title.narrative: Strengthening Women’s Role in Transformational Adaptation to Climate Change: Gaps and Challenges

description.narrative: In Their Lifetime (ITL) driven by creating impactful changes within a generation, emphasizes women's empowerment at the forefront of climate action and strengthening women's role in transformational adaptation. Under the ITL programme, Christian Aid Bangladesh, in partnership with CPRD, is implementing a project in Kurigram, under which women of climate-afflicted families have been supported with small-scale blended finance (grants plus microcredit) and training on climate resilient IGAs to increase their families’ economic resilience to climate change. However, during the mid-term investigation, it was observed that women in a number of families did not have functional authority of the operation of the IGAs they were supported for. This proves that only finance and skills cannot empower women to utilize their full potential for climate adaptation. There are various structural, socio-economic, socio-cultural factors that hinder women’s agency for climate adaptation. Hence, their true potential for climate adaptation remains under-utilized in our country. This project will generate research-based insights that will inform interventions aimed at supporting women’s climate adaptation actions and develop a set of strategies and policies to ensure a range of support mechanism for the full realization of women’s potential for climate adaptation at the family and community level. This study will apply a mixed-method approach and collect both quantitative and qualitative data, offering a comprehensive understanding of the measurable outcome and the deeper context-specific insight. The data collection methods will include questionnaire survey, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, in-depth interviews, and consultation. It will delve into findings to better understand the pre-requisites and factors of women’s empowerment and their economic and financial management towards climate actions, especially during different seasons and disasters. Finally, the research will put recommendations for relevant government organizations to formulate and reform policies that help utilize women’s full potential for climate adaptation.
